ACTEA  RACEMOSA.*

Actea  raeemosa,  Linnee.     Black  Coliosh.     Ranunculacece.


Grows  in  woodlands  from  Canada  to  Florida.  Famous  as  a  popular
medicine,  particularly  for  snake-bites.  Has  received  so  many  improper
names  that  the  oldest  one  is  preferred.  Proved  in  1853  by  H.  M.  Paine,  in
1858  by  Ch.  H.  Burr,  in  1859  by  Hill  and  Douglas,  in  1871  by  Bacmeister,
and  used  like  a  polychrest  by  most  practitioners.
